title: When do starred modified Macdonald polynomials equal the unstarred ones?
question: Let $\lambda$ be a partition with $\lambda_n=0$ and let $S_n(\lambda)$ be the content-fixed sector appearing in the multispecies CTMC construction for modified Macdonald polynomials. For $x_i>0$ and $0\le t<1$ the proposed stationary law is $\pi(\mu)=F_{\mu}^*(x;1,t)/P_{\lambda}^*(x;1,t)$, where $P_{\lambda}^*(x;1,t)=\sum_{\nu\in S_n(\lambda)}F_{\nu}^*(x;1,t)$. Most references assert without proof that the starred specialization differs from the unstarred modified Macdonald $F_{\mu}(x;1,t)$ only by an explicit product in the parts of $\mu$. Could someone explain precisely when $F_{\mu}^*=F_{\mu} \cdot c_{\mu}(t)$ and how that ratio guarantees that the CTMC stationary weights patch from the local (single site) normalization to the global sector sum?

nodes.text: for all \mu\in S_n(\lambda) with x_i>0, 0\le t<1
if multiplicities m_i(\mu) are finite then starred/unstarred differ by \prod (t;t)_{m_i}^{-1}
